basic_identification.full_title: Organic No Bake (Self Setting) Binders for Use in Foundries — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering / Foundry and Steel Castings

sectional_committee.name: Foundry and Steel Casting Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the physical, chemical, and mechanical performance requirements, classification, sampling guidelines, and testing procedures for organic no-bake (self-setting) liquid binders used to bond sand in foundry mold and core-making processes. These binders react with chemical hardeners or catalysts at room temperature to cure without the application of heat, facilitating high-dimensional accuracy in molten metal castings.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike builders hardware or metal packaging containers which are under strict statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), industrial foundry binders and accessories under IS 10032 : 2013 are certified on a voluntary basis. Conforming manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under Scheme-I of Schedule-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Compliance is routinely mandated inside public and private sector foundry, metallurgy, and heavy casting procurement tenders. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial foundry resin binders.

requirements.detail: The organic binder must be supplied in a liquid state, typically formulated from furan resins (based on furfuryl alcohol), phenolic resins, or alkyd systems. The specific chemistry dictates the corresponding acid catalyst or hardener system required for room-temperature curing.
To ensure uniform pumpability and rapid, consistent mixing with sand grains, the viscosity must not exceed specified limits when tested via standard viscometers (such as Ford Cup viscometry at 30°C).
Prescribes a minimum percentage of non-volatile active resin solids to ensure that the binder provides sufficient dry strength after the carrier solvents evaporate.

For binders intended for steel or high-grade iron castings, the nitrogen content is strictly restricted. High nitrogen levels can decompose under casting temperatures and dissolve into the liquid steel, causing pinhole porosity and structural casting defects.

requirements.requirement_type: Bench Life and Strip Time of Sand Mix
requirements.detail: The binder system, when mixed with standard sand and catalyst, must provide a usable bench life (pot life) to allow core box packing, followed by a controlled strip time (setting time) after which the core gains sufficient green strength to be safely stripped.

The fully cured sand core must not evolve excessive gas when exposed to molten metal temperatures. Evolved gas volume must remain within restricted limits (such as 16 to 20 ml/g max) to prevent gas blowholes in castings.

All binders of the same grade, type, and batch manufactured under essentially similar conditions in a single day constitute one inspection lot. Random samples are selected for both physical sand-mix tests and wet chemical/referee analyses. Non-conforming lots must be isolated and rejected.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10032 : 2013 is the national Indian Standard specification governing organic no-bake (self-setting) liquid binders used in foundry sand molding and core-making processes. Unlike thermal-cure core binders or clay-bonded green sands, organic no-bake binders are mixed with silica sand and a chemical catalyst (or co-binder hardener) to cure spontaneously at room temperature without requiring baking ovens. This standard establishes rigorous guidelines to ensure that binders possess the physical and chemical properties required to support heavy molten metal castings without structural deformation, mold collapse, or chemical contamination. It regulates viscosity, specific gravity, solids content, and limits nitrogen content to prevent gas-induced pinhole porosity in steel castings. Additionally, it mandates that sand-mix specimens satisfy strict mechanical benchmarks—including early handling strength (e.g., 0.010 MPa within 15 minutes) and a robust final cured compression strength of at least 1.72 MPa—alongside strict control of evolved gas volumes during casting to eliminate blowhole defects.
